content: The medication is indicated for the treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis when used in combination with one or more antituberculosis drugs. Initial Phase (2 months): Administer 600 mg orally twice weekly for 2 months. Ensure the interval between doses is not less than 3 days. This regimen must be combined with other antituberculosis drugs. Continuation Phase (4 months): Administer 600 mg orally once weekly for 4 months under direct observation therapy, in combination with isoniazid or another appropriate antituberculosis drug. The medication is also indicated for the treatment of latent TB infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis in adults and children aged 2 years or older who are at high risk of progression to active TB disease. This includes individuals in close contact with active TB patients, those with recent conversion to a positive tuberculin skin test, HIV-infected patients, or individuals with pulmonary fibrosis evident on radiographs. Safety and efficacy in children under 2 years of age have not been established. Drug Interactions and Contraindications: 1. Artemether/Lumefantrine: Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to reduced serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. 2. Cariprazine: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of cariprazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. CYP3A4 is responsible for the formation and elimination of cariprazine's active metabolites, and the net effect of CYP3A4 inducers on cariprazine exposure is unclear. 3. Cobicistat: Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers may reduce cobicistat systemic exposure by over 80%, significantly reducing its efficacy. 4. Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of these contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest as contraception while on strong CYP3A4 inducers due to decreased contraceptive efficacy. These contraceptives should not be used for at least 28 days after discontinuation of the inducer. 5. Doravirine: Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of doravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to reduced plasma concentrations, loss of virologic response, and potential resistance to doravirine. 6. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Rifapentine reduces the therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Rifapentine decreases the levels of this combination therapy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and potential resistance. 8. Fostemsavir: Rifapentine reduces the levels of fostemsavir (a prodrug) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to decreased plasma concentrations of its active moiety, temsavir. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of sofosbuvir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration is contraindicated as it decreases conversion to sofosbuvir's active metabolite, responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. 11. Lonafarnib: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 12. Lorlatinib: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Discontinue the strong CYP3A inducer for three plasma half-lives before initiating lorlatinib. 13. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended as it may reduce the effectiveness of lumacaftor/ivacaftor. 14. Lurasidone: Rifapentine decreases the levels of lurasidone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Mavacamten: Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of mavacamten by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. If unavoidable, increase enzalutamide dose from 160 mg daily to 240 mg daily.
